item: engine_text is one call to the shared scrub; stopword_batch --apply files foreign-script words in _multilingual.yml
key_paths: src/monitoring/engine_text.py src/backup/merge.py src/monitoring/keyword_write_cost.py tests/test_engine_text.py scripts/stopword_batch.py tests/test_stopword_batch.py
summary: engine_text (the cleaned engine text in the re-index job, the keyword cleanup and write-cost records, the backlog reason) now calls secret_scrub.exception_text: every held passphrase (session, OO_DB_PASSPHRASE and the signing-key one the old loop missed), every shape, the cut after, a passphrase under the floor or a UnicodeError by class only; the import stays inside the function so the index engine stamp is unchanged. Log lines name the class beside the words. The AST guard counts engine_text bindings, refuses bare and aliased traceback readers, checks the helper bodies and has refusal tests; a shapes x forms test asserts on the encoded stretch of 4 passphrases in 9 forms, with cuts inside it (a scrub of the typed secret alone fails 13 cells). stopword_batch --apply splits a batch by the guard's script map and files a Latin word of a non-Latin log in _multilingual.yml, preparing both files before writing either (temporary files, then renames).
